title.narrative: Humanitarian Assistance to South Sudanese refugees, Sudanese IDPs and Sudanese Host Communities

description.narrative: Improved living conditions of conflict affected South Sudanese Refugees, Internally displaced persons and vulnerable host community members.

South Sudanese Refugee(SSR) crisis remains the fastest growing and largest refugee situation on the African continent since the onset of conflict in South Sudan in 2013. The Sudan 2018 Humanitarian Overview estimates that over 455,000 SSR have arrived in Sudan as of October 2017 with an additional 200,000 SSR expected by the end of 2018. Based on most recent assessment conducted by UNHCR and the Commissioner for Refugees (COR) in June 2018, a total of 13,070 SSR is hosted in Al Lait and El Fasher Localities in North Darfur. Internally displaced people from Eastern Darfur face similar humanitarian challenges like the SSR. 7,554 IDPs were hosted by relatives in four villages in Al Lait locality as of February 2018. The project is focusing on improving access to water, household latrines and hygiene products; improving food and nutrition security as well as improving access to shelter and basic Non-Food-Items by the target group.
The project directly targets 16,744 individuals composed of South Sudanese Refugees, IDPs and most vulnerable host community members.
